trust_decision.summary: Whether an iframe src belongs to an admin-allowlisted origin, where a '*' wildcard in the allowlist entry is turned into a regex character class that must not cross the URL authority boundary; decided in the JS markdown sanitizer for cooked posts and in the Ruby onebox origin-regex builder for oneboxed/oEmbed HTML.

landing_point.why: The summary names the 'iframe origin allowlist' (site setting allowed_iframes); searching allowedIframes leads straight to the JS sanitizer's wildcard-to-regex replace, which is the only consumer of allowed_iframes in the frontend (frontend/discourse-markdown-it/src/options.js:68).

fix_sites.entry_point: POST/PUT /posts (config/routes.rb:1254) raw markdown cooked via PrettyText.cook (lib/pretty_text.rb:318), plus client composer preview
fix_sites.module_kind: shared JS sanitizer library (pretty-text addon, runs client-side and server-side)

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /posts with a bare URL that is oneboxed (oEmbed iframe), and GET /onebox (config/routes.rb:1628 -> app/controllers/onebox_controller.rb:28)
fix_sites.module_kind: Ruby onebox library: origin-to-regex builder consumed by Matcher, Preview sanitizer and AllowlistedGenericOnebox

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: lib/onebox/engine.rb:30 (Ruby) vs frontend/pretty-text/addon/sanitizer.js:149 (JS); the Ruby regex is consumed at lib/onebox/sanitize_config.rb:71-73, lib/onebox/matcher.rb:32-35, lib/onebox/engine/allowlisted_generic_onebox.rb:198 and :238

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The Ruby onebox builder already excludes / ? # (lib/onebox/engine.rb:30, covered by spec/lib/onebox/engine_spec.rb:77-90 from an earlier fix), so a solver landing in JS can argue oneboxes are 'already hardened' and a separate oEmbed pipeline; conversely a solver landing in Ruby adds only the backslash and misses that JS still uses [^/]+ with no ? or # exclusion.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Wildcard entries must still allow legitimate multi-level subdomains (https://deep.embed.example.com/player for https://*.example.com/) and ports on pure-origin entries; replacing the wildcard with a single-label class or requiring an exact host breaks this (fix.diff:128-132, spec/lib/onebox/engine_spec.rb:80-82).

O6_input_shapes: authority ended by '/' (JS only; Ruby already handled)
authority ended by '?' (JS; Ruby already handled)
authority ended by '#' (JS; Ruby already handled)
authority ended by literal backslash (both JS and Ruby)
percent-encoded src: JS tests both decoded and raw value (frontend/pretty-text/addon/sanitizer.js:135-153)

O7_producer.where: lib/oneboxer.rb:476-480 merges allowed_onebox_iframes and allowed_iframes (and expands '*' to all engine origins) before lib/oneboxer.rb:253 and lib/onebox/preview.rb:20-21 compile them via origins_to_regexes; JS gets the list from frontend/discourse-markdown-it/src/options.js:68

O8b_injection_room.sibling: is_embedded? could compare the oEmbed iframe host with its own wildcard/suffix host match instead of the shared allowed_iframe_regexes
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same class already does its own host matching with host_matches for html_providers (lib/onebox/engine/allowlisted_generic_onebox.rb:232-233), so a maintainer could plausibly reuse it for the iframe src.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: engine selection could check engine iframe_origins with a local wildcard-to-regex conversion
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Matcher compares origin strings against regexes; a local helper that expands '*' with [^/]+ like the JS code would look natural there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a planted iframe-origin check reusing WildcardDomainChecker (wildcard becomes \S*)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is an existing project helper for wildcard host allowlists, so a maintainer could reuse it for iframe hosts; it does not stop at the authority.

O9_family: origin/allowlist validation (CWE-346): wildcard host pattern crosses URL authority boundary, a parser differential between the regex and the browser URL parser

O10_build.toolchain: Ruby/Bundler with RSpec; Node/pnpm with Ember QUnit (bin/qunit) for frontend unit tests
O10_build.project_tests: spec/lib/onebox/engine_spec.rb (origins_to_regexes, offline unit), frontend/discourse/tests/unit/lib/sanitizer-test.js (QUnit, needs a headless browser), spec/requests/posts_controller_spec.rb (needs DB+Redis, WebMock-stubbed oEmbed)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add only the backslash to the Ruby class (or only fix JS [^/]+ -> [^/?#]+), leaving the other implementation or the backslash shape open.
